sources.title: If you really hate it when music and film stars do politics, here’s the answer: give us politics that works | Nesrine Malik
sources.description: The problem is not famous people speaking out, as they always have. It is the feeling that leaders have failed, obliging celebrities to fill the vacuum Every time a public figure in entertainment speaks up about politics in a way deemed “controversial”, it is as if it’s the first time that has ever happened. The outrage is fresh; critics rediscover and announce, as if they have just captured an elusive, profound notion, that art should be separate from politics. A form of disciplining is dispensed. Please, Mr or Miss Moneybags, with your preening notions that you have anything intelligent or informed to say about immigration policy or Palestine. Stick to football. Stick to pop music. Stick to acting. Stick to children’s shows. Even at a time when a political moment has engulfed everything, this response continues to be born again, without regard for history or ability to confront rupture. The horror of Gaza has broken the art world , roiled Hollywood , fractured literary institutions . And still, as Ed Sheeran stands alone on stage following the withdrawal of all his support acts (in solidarity with Macklemore, who was removed from the tour due to a pro-Palestinian speech), he told his audience that he wants his music to be “about unity, not division”. The speed at which his tour unravelled is not evidence of the incompatibility of music and politics, necessitating that they remain separate to avoid that “division”. It is a study in how it is becoming increasingly unnatural to separate them. Continue reading...

sources.description: 近日，日本防卫省公布了2027财年防卫预算申请概要。同往年相比，这份文件主打“以防卫力变革为目标”，突出特点是防卫预算申请额再创新高，“新型作战方式”比重上升，并提出所谓“防卫与经济的良性循环”。这些看似专业的名词背后，反映的是日本防卫政策和军事野心的加速扩张。
